bug_semantics: PickleScan classified a pickle only from GLOBAL/INST/STACK_GLOBAL module-and-name references found in its opcode stream. A malicious pickle could import the unblocked pkgutil.resolve_name, call it by REDUCE with data such as 'os:system' to obtain a blocked callable without importing that callable, then invoke the returned callable with a second REDUCE. Because REDUCE arguments and returned stack values were not resolved into new globals, the scanner saw only pkgutil.resolve_name and reported no dangerous global while unpickling executed arbitrary code.
flaw_origin: Commit c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e created the scanner, its finite _suspicious_globals blocklist, the _list_globals routine that extracts only direct GLOBAL and STACK_GLOBAL references, and scan_pickle_bytes' table-membership decision. That initial design first made indirect callable resolution through an unlisted resolver such as pkgutil.resolve_name invisible; later table growth retained the same flaw until pkgutil.resolve_name was explicitly blocked.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object names human author and committer Matthieu Maitre <mmaitre314@users.noreply.github.com>, has the message 'Implement Pickle scanner', and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailer.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/security/advisories/GHSA-vvpj-8cmc-gx39 describes the two-REDUCE chain: pkgutil.resolve_name('os:system') returns os.system and the next REDUCE invokes it; the only imported global visible to PickleScan is the previously unblocked pkgutil.resolve_name. It declares affected versions <1.0.4 and patched version 1.0.4.

git show c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e:src/picklescan/scanner.py and git blame -L 13,102 at that commit show the BIC creating _suspicious_globals at lines 14-23, extracting only GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL at lines 49-74, and counting an issue only when the extracted pair matches the table at lines 77-90. pkgutil is absent from the table.

git log --all --reverse -S'_suspicious_globals' -- src/picklescan/scanner.py identifies c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e as the first addition. The commit is a single-parent implementation commit, not a move, refactor, revert, release-only commit, or squash aggregate requiring decomposition.

git show -s reports the BIC's immediate parent as 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326. Direct parent-tree verification with git ls-tree -r --name-only 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326 -- src/picklescan/scanner.py returns no path; listing that parent tree shows no src directory, so the vulnerable scanner mechanism is absent there.

The BIC's setup.cfg declares version 0.0.1, and git tag --contains shows it in every repository release tag from v0.0.2 through vulnerable v1.0.3 and later. This places the introducer before the advisory's entire affected range.

git diff b9997634683a4f4bd0c7e3701e7ce7e90fe70e8c bf26452ae2e3204429762c2bb1aa9eacd40436bb -- src/picklescan/scanner.py shows the direct fix adding '"pkgutil": {"resolve_name"}' to _unsafe_globals; git blame at the fixed tree attributes that line (src/picklescan/scanner.py:199) to bf26452ae2e3204429762c2bb1aa9eacd40436bb.

git rev-parse verifies v1.0.3 is b9997634683a4f4bd0c7e3701e7ce7e90fe70e8c, v1.0.4 is bf26452ae2e3204429762c2bb1aa9eacd40436bb, and the fix commit's parent is exactly the v1.0.3 commit. The same fix changes setup.cfg from 1.0.3 to 1.0.4 and adds a GHSA-vvpj-8cmc-gx39 regression fixture/assertion.

git cat-file -p c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e provides the only AI-attribution evidence considered: human author/committer identity, plain implementation message, and no trailers or bot marker.
reasoning: The lifecycle begins with the first scanner implementation in c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e: it introduced both the blocklist security model and the direct-global-only extraction/lookup that accepts any unlisted global. That is the smallest real BIC because its parent has no scanner source at all, while later changes merely renamed or expanded the table and refined parsing without creating the indirect-resolution blind spot. The attack imports only pkgutil.resolve_name, passes a blocked target's module:name as ordinary pickle data, and chains REDUCE so the dangerous callable never appears as a GLOBAL opcode. Commit bf26452ae2e3204429762c2bb1aa9eacd40436bb directly closes this reported gadget by adding pkgutil.resolve_name to the unsafe table, and it is exactly the v1.0.4 boundary immediately after v1.0.3. The BIC commit object contains no AI authorship or co-authorship signal, so later activity and any evidence associated only with the fix cannot attribute the original flaw; the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
